cards.back: An integral defined using a limit because of an infinite interval or an unbounded integrand.
An accumulated exposure measure given by integrating concentration over time.
A series Σ1/nᵖ; it converges exactly when p>1.
A bound or expression for the error left after truncating a Taylor expansion.
Accumulated mechanical energy transfer W=∫F·dx along a displacement.
The integral of a function over an interval divided by interval length.
Distance from a power-series center within which the series converges; endpoints need separate tests.
The error between a function and its finite Taylor polynomial, bounded using higher derivatives.
Total = ∫ rate dt; units: (amount/time) × time.
T = h[q₀/2 + … + qₙ/2]; S = (h/3)[q₀ + 4q₁ + 2q₂ + … + qₙ] with n even.
|E| ≤ (b − a)h²/12 · max|f″|; convex functions are overestimated; halving h quarters the bound.
∫₀^∞ e^(−kt) dt = 1/k converges; ∫₁^∞ dt/t diverges; ∫₁^∞ dt/t² converges.
Pₙ(x) = Σ f⁽ᵏ⁾(a)(x − a)ᵏ/k! for k ≤ n.
|Rₙ| ≤ M|x − a|ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1)! with M bounding |f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾| on the interval.
1 − e^(−kt) ≈ kt with relative error about kt/2.
ln(1 + x) ≈ x and sin θ ≈ θ (radians) only for small arguments.
Substitution reverses the chain rule; parts reverses the product rule; partial fractions separates a rational integrand after division if needed.
Transform both endpoint bounds or return to the original variable before evaluating. Keep domains and units consistent.
Differentiate a candidate primitive and compare it with the original integrand; check poles separately.
ln|x| has derivative 1/x on each nonzero interval; it does not justify endpoint cancellation across zero.
Integrate on a finite nonsingular interval and take the required endpoint limit. Every improper part must converge separately.
∫₁∞x⁻ᵖ converges for p>1; ∫₀¹x⁻ᵖ converges for p<1.
A convergent nonnegative upper bound guarantees convergence below it; a divergent lower bound guarantees divergence above it.
Symmetric cancellation is a separate definition. It does not replace convergence of each ordinary improper part.
aₙ→0 is necessary for Σaₙ to converge but not sufficient; inspect partial sums or use a justified test.
A limiting absolute ratio below 1 gives absolute convergence; above 1 gives divergence; equal to 1 is inconclusive.
For indices 0 through N and |r|<1, the exact tail is r^(N+1)/(1−r). Count indices explicitly.
For positive decreasing f with a convergent tail, ∫_(N+1)∞f≤Σ_(n=N+1)∞f(n)≤∫_N∞f.
Absolute convergence means Σ|aₙ| converges. Conditional convergence means the signed series converges while the magnitudes do not.
For nonnegative decreasing magnitudes tending to zero, the error after N terms is at most the first omitted magnitude.
Under those conditions, the exact sum lies between consecutive partial sums; the remainder has the first omitted sign.
A bound that fails a tolerance is inconclusive about actual error. A successful bound is deterministic, not a confidence interval.
The radius defines interior absolute convergence. Test each real endpoint separately to determine brackets.
Power series can be integrated and differentiated inside their radius; endpoints can change convergence behavior.
Track x−c, normalized arguments and the first term when shifting indices or substituting variables.
A function may be defined outside an expansion radius; its finite polynomial is evaluable there but need not approximate it.
The coefficient of (x−a)ʲ is f^(j)(a)/j!. Degree and number of nonzero terms are distinct.
Bound the next derivative over the entire interval connecting center and evaluation point, then multiply by distance power divided by factorial.
A pointwise bound B(x) yields accumulated error at most ∫B; output units include the interval units.
Separate truncation, rounding, uncertain inputs and model discrepancy. A Taylor remainder controls only the stated mathematical truncation.
Area uses strip or sector area; volume uses cross-sectional area or shells; arc length uses √((x′)²+(y′)²)dt.
A radial cross-sectional integral needs 2πr dr. Dividing by πR² gives an area average.
Parametric length counts the traced distance over the specified bounds, including repeated traversals.
Cross-sectional integration of a volumetric concentration gives amount per length; a cylinder length is required for total amount.
Integrate force over displacement; composite rules need the correct spacing and weights. N·m is J.
On a valid interval, bound the exact remaining integrand and integrate that bound. Positive omitted terms give an underestimate.
A constant force offset contributes offset times displacement to work. Averaging balanced repeats does not remove it.
Agreement with a known synthetic generating formula checks the calculation, not whether a real device follows that model.
